analysis: The bias-free model completed successfully, resolving the reported scoring-consistency crash. Training and both candidate-scoring branches use raw dot products with the shared item embeddings. Validation HR@10 was 0.665, NDCG@10 was 0.428823, and the best epoch was 15 of 35 completed epochs. No comparison result is provided, so a ranking improvement from removing biases cannot be established.
code_summary: Causal NextItNet with 64-dimensional shared item embeddings, maximum sequence length 128, and eight residual blocks using dilations [1,2,4,8,1,2,4,8]. Each block gates between local and dilated kernel-3 convolutions, then applies a second dilated convolution, with pre-layer normalization, GELU, dropout 0.2, and learned per-channel residual scales initialized to 0.1. Padding is masked throughout. Candidate scoring uses the last nonpadding representation and supports shared or per-sequence candidates. No item biases. LR=0.001, weight decay=0.00001, batch size=128.
